files.name: CHANGELOG.md
files.body:
Models get easier to work with together and to show off. A Parts panel lists a model's parts as a tree to hide, isolate and find them, and IFC buildings show each element's properties. View in AR puts the model in your room at its real size, on an iPhone, an iPad or an Android phone. A link to a model in Talk, Text, Collectives or Deck now shows as a card, and the Smart Picker can insert one. When someone adds a note to a model, its owner and the people who wrote notes on it are notified, and the Activity stream records it.

### Added
- Parts: a new section in the tools panel lists the model's parts as a tree, so assemblies can be worked on part by part. Choose a part to tint it in the model, hide it or show it again, show only that part (Isolate), or move the camera to it (Zoom to). Click a part in the model and it is chosen in the list, with the rows above it opened. A filter finds parts by name anywhere in the tree, and Show all brings everything back. Parts with no name are called "Mesh 3" or "Group 2" (with their material's name beside them when they have one), and a chain of groups with one thing in each is one row. The list is made as it is opened and draws only the rows in view, so a building with thousands of elements opens as quickly as a bracket. It works from the keyboard as a tree: arrow keys move, Right and Left open and close, Enter chooses, and H, I and Z hide, isolate and zoom. A hidden part stays hidden through Clay, Normals and X-ray and while Exploded view moves the parts, and cannot be measured or clicked; exports and thumbnails still show every part. A scan or a splat has no parts, and its Parts row says so.
- IFC files list their elements under the storey, building or space that holds them, named as the file names them, and choosing an element shows its type, storey and property sets and quantities, read from the file when it is chosen.
- View in AR: on an iPhone or iPad, "View in AR" in the tools panel's Export section opens the model in AR Quick Look, and on an Android phone with Chrome it shows the model over the camera: point at the floor, tap to place it, tap somewhere else to move it, and Exit AR to leave. Either way the model is its real size, taken from the file's unit (a 100 mm part is 100 mm on your table, a glTF is in metres). The button shows only on phones and tablets that can do this, so desktops don't see it; it is off for scans and splats, with a note saying why, and a model past a million triangles on an iPhone (three million on Android) is turned down with a message instead of running the phone out of memory. The AR code loads only when the button is pressed. View in AR is in the full viewer; the lighter viewer that public links and the Files preview open does not offer it yet.
- Notifications and Activity for notes: when someone adds a note to a model, its owner and everyone who has written a note on it before get a notification ("Sara added a note on bracket.stl"), which opens the model with that note in focus. A run of notes by one person on one model, each within ten minutes of the last, is one notification that counts them ("Sara added 4 notes"). Nobody is told about their own notes, and someone who can no longer open the model is not told at all. Adding, changing and deleting notes also shows in the Activity stream of everyone who can open the model, under a new "3D Viewer" filter and on the file's Activity tab; an author still typing a note they have just added does not fill the stream. Notifications and stream entries name the person and the file, never what the note says. Under Settings › Notifications, the "3D Viewer" activity can be turned off for the stream, or on for email. A notification about one note goes away when the note is deleted, and any notification goes away when its model is deleted or you can no longer open it.
- Links to a model now show as a card in Talk, Text, Collectives, Deck and the other apps that draw link previews: the model's thumbnail, its name, its format and size, and an "Open in 3D Viewer" button. A link copied with "Copy link to this view" says so on its card and opens at that view. Only people who can open the file see the card; for everyone else the link stays a plain link. The Smart Picker has a "3D models" entry that finds a model by name and inserts its link.

### Changed
- three.js r186 → r187, three-mesh-bvh 0.9.16 → 0.9.18, `@nextcloud/vue` 9.13.1 → 9.14.0 and `@nextcloud/dialogs` 7.5.0 → 8.0.0. Dialogs 8's file picker uses the breadcrumbs and empty state the file browser already had in a chunk of its own, so that chunk is now part of the main app chunk; the page loads no more than before.
- Every pull request now opens STL, STEP and 3DM models, a public link, link previews and note notifications in a browser against a real Nextcloud, with the app installed in `custom_apps` as App Store installs have it, and fails on any blocked script or missing app file. This is the kind of problem behind issues #169, #188, #204 and #211.

### Fixed
- On a phone, the Export button at the end of the tools panel's export row was cut off at the panel's right edge. The row was its own padding wider than the panel.

### Security
- Cleared the `minimatch` globparts DoS ([GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249)) from the production graph: `overrides.webdav.minimatch` moves from `^10.2.3` to `^11.0.1`, taking `npm audit --omit=dev` from six moderate to zero. `webdav` only matches globs when a directory listing is asked for with one, which neither the viewer nor `@nextcloud/files` does, and the browser bundle uses `webdav`'s prebuilt web build, whose own copy no lockfile change reaches.
